reason: The passage portrays the regular people unfavorably. They are depicted as disobedient and faithless: they go out to gather manna on the Sabbath despite God's explicit instructions not to do so (וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י יָצְא֥וּ מִן־ הָעָ֖ם לִלְקֹ֑ט וְלֹ֖א מָצָֽאוּ׃), failing to trust that God has already provided. God then directly rebukes them, asking 'How long will you refuse to keep my commandments and laws?' (עַד־ אָ֙נָה֙ מֵֽאַנְתֶּ֔ם לִשְׁמֹ֥ר מִצְוֺתַ֖י וְתוֹרֹתָֽי׃). The narrative emphasizes their resistance, disobedience, and lack of faith rather than commending their character or actions.
